# Psalm 110 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A psalm of David. The LORD said to my Lord: 'Sit in the place of honor at my right hand until I turn your enemies into your footrest.'

**2** The LORD will extend your powerful scepter from Zion. Rule right in the middle of your enemies!

**3** Your people will volunteer freely when you lead them into battle, dressed in holy splendor. Your young warriors will come to you fresh as the morning dew.

**4** The LORD has made an unbreakable oath: 'You are a priest forever — in the same tradition as Melchizedek.'

**5** The Lord stands at your right hand; he will crush kings on the day of his fury.

**6** He will judge the nations, piling up the dead. He will crush the ruler of the whole earth.

**7** The king will drink from the stream along the way, and then lift his head in triumph.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **110:1**: This is the single most important messianic psalm in the entire Bible. Jesus himself quoted it to prove that the Messiah is more than just a human descendant of David — he's David's Lord. The NT references it more than any other OT verse.

- **110:4**: A priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek — not Aaron. This mysterious figure from Genesis 14 had no recorded genealogy, which made him the perfect type for a priesthood that transcends Israel's Levitical system. The book of Hebrews builds its entire theology of Jesus' priesthood on this single verse.

— PNEUMA
